- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 3–8% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% upward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
